source_clarification.before: CLD Corollary 15.2.9 states: if $X$ is locally holomorphically separated, $F\subset X$ is closed and countable at infinity (in particular compact), and $U_i$ is an ordinary open cover of $F$, there are nonnegative ordinary smooth $\theta_i$, each compactly supported inside $U_i$, locally finite, with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ near $F$. Only finite covers of compact sets are used.
source_clarification.after: For a compact subset $F$ and a finite ordinary open cover $(U_i)$ of $F$, there are nonnegative ordinary smooth $\theta_i$, each compactly supported inside $U_i$, with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ near $F$. This compact specialization follows from CLD Corollary 15.2.5 and ordinary smooth functional calculus. For each $x\in F$, apply 15.2.5 with $\{x\}\subset U_i$ to obtain a smooth function equal to one near $x$ and compactly supported in $U_i$. Compose with a nonnegative smooth real function equal to zero near zero and equal to one near one, obtaining a nonnegative bump with the same support containment. Compactness selects finitely many such bumps; group them by cover index into $\psi_i$, and put $s=\sum_i\psi_i$. Then $s>0$ near $F$. Apply 15.2.5 again to compact $F$ inside the open $\{s>0\}$, and the same nonnegative composition, to obtain $\chi$ compactly supported there and equal to one near $F$. Set $\theta_i=\chi\psi_i/s$ on that open and extend by zero. Smoothness follows since the support of $\chi$ lies compactly inside the open. Each $\theta_i$ has compact support inside $U_i$ and their sum is $\chi$. No arbitrary countable-at-infinity, fixed-cover-index compact-support assertion is used. Only this compact-set, finite-cover version is needed.
source_clarification.reason: Source-citation compact specialization; no theorem or actual use changed

result.report:
The supplied argument establishes Theorems A–C under their stated hypotheses, including every ordinary compact test, singular and nonreduced structures, and finite towers whose individual quadratic stages satisfy (H). Original P06.2 recognition is not established and is not required for this audit. No prior verdict, compilation result, diagnostic, or artifact hash was used as mathematical evidence.

I inspected the specified CLD v2 and GR v2 primary statements and the relevant proof bodies. The external inputs below retain their actual hypotheses. In particular, ordinary moment representations use ordinary open covers; Euclidean extension uses the closed-in-an-ambient-open condition; calibration degrees retain Artinian lengths; scalar projection and restriction of the ground field have different normalizations. GJR weakly smooth descent and Conrad–Temkin morphism descent are not imported as ordinary-form descent results.

The finite-algebra foundation is sound. The supplied induction proves equivalence with a coefficient norm over a complete field, so the finite completed tensor is the algebraic tensor with its finite-module topology. Tensor exactness gives B^σ=A without field-valued averaging, and invariant inverses descend. Spectral surjectivity justifies the unit criterion without reducedness. The quadratic fibre algebra is a field or a product of two fields; finite-dimensional norm equivalence proves uniqueness of its extending absolute values. The idempotent argument establishes transitivity of the involution on fibre points. The Hausdorffness, compact inverse-image, and compact-complement shrinking arguments are valid and always retain the whole fibre. They do not require a topological covering.

The purity proof also works. A point with kernel a minimal prime belongs only to that minimal component, establishing its dimension n. The nilradical is nilpotent; after tensoring, the injection into the finite product of fraction-field tensors proves that the reduced tensor is reduced. Its minimal primes contract to downstairs minimal primes. The supplied determinant, going-up, and incomparability arguments prove dimension preservation for the resulting finite integral domain extensions. Thus upstairs local dimension is n everywhere. Reduction is used here only to identify components, not to replace integration calibrations. The common rational-domain presentations justify the same-carrier ordinary sheaf identification under finite restriction of the ground field, including differentials and supports.

For Theorem A, (H) gives all three trace rows norm-one entries and norm-one pairwise determinants. Therefore at least two traces attain max(|f|,|σf|). At a singleton fibre the two unit traces can be retained after one shrink. Identity (4) holds throughout that neighbourhood: unequal norms prohibit cancellation; equal norms allow cancellation in at most one selected trace, leaving the product zero. Pair products then give all δ_iδ_j. These arguments include characteristic two; every division by two occurs over the real coefficient algebra.

The differential reconstruction supplies the additional generators actually needed. On each tripod ray, U dV−V dU restricts to zero; at the vertex its coefficients vanish. The compact-image nullity criterion establishes this as an ordinary sheaf identity. Expanding it gives (7), and adding its conjugate gives exactly (10), including the alternating term. Every zero case is covered: v_i(x₀)=0 forces δ_i=0 after shrinking, while e_ij(x₀)=0 forces δ_i=δ_j. In the remaining cases every logarithmic argument is a unit. Consequently (11)–(12) descend δ_i dδ_j. Unit logarithms have zero mixed Hessian as forms, so differentiation gives all three kinds of differential pairs in (13), including nonsymmetric mixed pairs. Even-parity polynomial/exterior monomials are generated by these pairs and the invariant norm coordinates, with the required graded signs. The auxiliary unit list and shrink depend only on the original finite list and its pair products, not on polynomial degree. This establishes every bidegree in Theorem A.

For Theorem B, the singleton construction first extends the coefficient form to Euclidean space using the correct closed-subset hypothesis, then averages the entire superform, including differential factors. Gaussian convolution followed by polynomial kernel truncation gives uniform approximation through order two on the fixed box. Swap averaging preserves that control. On a two-point fibre, disjoint conjugate neighbourhoods and analytic gluing give an invariant unit tuple and an exact ordinary descendant. Neither construction invokes weakly smooth descent.

The replacement cutoff construction is valid in its exact compact, finite-cover scope. Point bumps, nonnegative functional calculus, and compactness give finitely many grouped functions ψ_i. Their sum s is positive near F. A second compact bump χ has support inside {s>0} and equals one near F. Hence θ_i=χψ_i/s extends smoothly by zero, has compact support inside U_i, and sums to one near F. All uses have compact F and finite covers: the image of supp β, and compact inverse images of cutoff supports. No assertion for a fixed cover index over a noncompact countable-at-infinity F is needed. Extension by zero in (16) is smooth because each product's support is compactly contained in its ordinary open. Formula (17) holds globally, including outside supp β. The enlarged moment lists, boxes, cutoffs, and support D are fixed independently of j.

The differentiated control is complete. For a fixed cutoff c and coefficient error e, d'd''(ce) has the four terms (d'd''c)e − d''c∧d'e + d'c∧d''e + c d'd''e. Fixed C² bounds on c and vanishing C² coefficient errors control every term. Unit-logarithmic differential basis factors are separately closed. In dimension n, the minor-vector calculation gives |Σ H_IJ v_Iv_J| ≤ binom(r,n) Mε Σ v_I². With the common top-degree ordering convention, the latter is contraction of the positive form ξⁿ/n!. Actual positive calibrations multiply both sides equally. Their compact tropical polyhedra have finitely many cells and finite weights, so the dominating measures are finite. If r<n the top form is zero. Summing on the finite cover proves the full signed-measure total-variation limit (19), not merely convergence of tropical integrals. Boundedness of h∘π on π⁻¹(D) then proves (20).

Theorem C follows for all compact ordinary (n−1,n−1) tests. On the restricted carrier, σ is a genuine K-analytic isomorphism of calibrated degree one. Restriction of the ground field multiplies calibration by 2; cancelling that factor proves invariance of the E-calibrated pairing. Real averaging therefore preserves the pairing and gives an invariant compact test. Scalar projection separately satisfies the no-degree-factor Radon pushforward formula, proving (22). Theorem B and total-variation convergence prove ascent; (22) alone proves descent. Ordinary opens preserve the needed local structure, purity and boundarylessness. Each finite quadratic stage preserves the ambient hypotheses, so iteration is legitimate without requiring the composite extension to be Galois.

passages.statement: CLD v2 §§11.1.1–2, 11.1.5–9 and 11.4.4: Over a complete non-Archimedean field k, the spectrum of a Banach algebra is compact Hausdorff and is nonempty when the algebra is nonzero. A k-affinoid algebra A is noetherian with closed ideals, and M(A)→Spec(A) is surjective. Rational affinoid neighbourhoods form a basis in an affinoid; affinoid neighbourhoods form a basis in a good analytic space; ordinary opens are analytic domains. Analytic functions form a sheaf and O(M(A))=A. Affinoid fibre products are computed by completed tensor products; scalar extension is M(A completed-tensor_k L), with surjective scalar projection for complete L/k. A finite Banach algebra over a k-affinoid algebra, equipped with its finite-module topology, is k-affinoid.

A finite Banach algebra over a k-affinoid algebra, equipped with its finite-module topology, is k-affinoid.

CLD v2 §11.2.2–3: Analytic separatedness implies topological separatedness. The dimension of a strict affinoid is its Krull dimension, scalar extension preserves analytic dimension, and for minimal-prime components X_i of an affinoid, dim_x X=max_{x∈X_i} dim X_i. Analytic domains preserve local dimension. Pure dimension n means dim_x X=n at every point.

CLD v2 Lemma 1.9.4, §§3.3.3, 3.3.11–12, Propositions 3.4.1 and 3.4.4, §§6.2.1–2, and Proposition 15.1.1(b): On a topologically separated analytic space, ordinary smooth (p,q)-forms admit moment pullback descriptions on ordinary open covers in every bidegree. A coefficient form on a paralinéaire subset P extends to an ambient open U when P is closed in U; the moment coefficient construction permits such a choice of U. Ordinary forms form an ordinary sheaf stable under smooth functional calculus, wedge, J, d′ and d″. Analytic pullbacks commute with these operations and the differentials satisfy the graded Leibniz rule. A moment coefficient form pulls back to zero in the G-form sheaf exactly when it restricts to zero on every compact-domain moment image; on compact charts the same criterion holds for the coefficient presheaf. Degree-zero forms inject into numerical functions.

CLD v2 Lemma 1.9.4, §§3.3.3, 3.3.11–12, Propositions 3.4.1 and 3.4.4, §§6.2.1–2, and Proposition 15.1.1(b): On a topologically separated analytic space, ordinary smooth (p,q)-forms admit moment pullback descriptions on ordinary open covers in every bidegree. A coefficient form on a paralinéaire subset P extends to an ambient open U when P is closed in U; the moment coefficient construction permits such a choice of U. Ordinary forms form an ordinary sheaf stable under smooth functional calculus, wedge, J, d′ and d″. Analytic pullbacks commute with these operations and the differentials satisfy the graded Leibniz rule. A moment coefficient form pulls back to zero in the G-form sheaf exactly when it restricts to zero on every compact-domain moment image; on compact charts the same criterion holds for the coefficient presheaf. CLD v2 §15.2.2 and Corollary 15.2.5: A good topologically separated analytic space is locally holomorphically separated. On a locally holomorphically separated analytic space X, for every compact subset F and ordinary open neighbourhood U of F, there exists an ordinary smooth function on X equal to one near F whose support is compact and contained in U.

CLD v2 §§5.4.4, 5.8.3–6, Proposition 5.10.1(c,d), §7.3.5, §§14.3.2–5, Theorem 15.7.1 and §15.7.2: A pure n-dimensional topologically separated analytic space, without a reducedness or smoothness hypothesis, has its canonical positive standard calibration and, with its analytic boundary, is a tropical space of level n; the induced structure on analytic domains agrees with their own analytic structure. Smooth top forms define locally finite calibrated Radon measures, and locally integrable multipliers define integration currents; continuous finite multipliers are locally integrable. Every compact tropical chart is pleasant, with tropical polyhedron the n-dimensional part of its image. For a locally integrable coefficient top form α on a pleasant chart f, f_trop,*((f*α)_Rad)=⟨α,μ_Πf⟩_Rad and integration is the corresponding calibrated contraction integral. Canonical cell calibrations use the positive finite degrees of local finite-flat torus projections and are standard, so smooth positive coefficient top forms have finite measure on compact charts.

CLD v2 §§13.3.1–5, Lemma 13.3.3, Proposition 14.3.6 and Proposition 15.3.1: For a compact zero-dimensional analytic fibre over x, its degree is the H(x)-dimension of its actual finite fibre algebra. After complete scalar extension, the degree at a fibre point equals the sum of degrees at its lifts over a specified lift of x. Calibrated degrees at quasi-finite generic points use the actual Artinian length ratio δ_A(M)=length_A(M)/length_A(A). For an analytic space of level n, a skeletal subset Σ with canonical calibration μ, and a complete extension L/k, its extended skeletal subset has canonical calibration μ_L satisfying π_*μ_L=μ. For a tropical-Borel (n,n) G-form ω, π_*(ω_L,Bor)=ω_Bor; when ω is locally integrable, π_*(ω_L,Rad)=ω_Rad. These scalar-projection equalities have no factor [L:k].

CLD v2 Remark 14.4.3 and Proposition 15.4.3 with §15.4.1: For finite F/k and an F-analytic space Z of level n, restriction of the ground field gives a k-analytic space Z₀ on the same carrier with the same dimension and skeletal subsets, and canonical calibration μ_Z₀=[F:k]μ_Z. If f:Y→X is a morphism between k-analytic spaces of level n, finite over the complement of a Zariski closed subset of X of dimension less than n, and ω is a locally integrable (p,n) G-form with p∈{n−1,n}, then f*ω is locally integrable and f_*((f*ω)_Rad)=dc(f)ω_Rad, where dc(f) is the calibrated degree. In particular an analytic isomorphism has calibrated degree one.

GR v2 §2.11(3′–5′): For an analytic domain V in an analytic space X, the relative analytic boundary ∂(V/X) is its topological boundary in X. For morphisms X→Y→S, ∂(X/S) is contained in ∂(X/Y)∪f⁻¹∂(Y/S). For any analytic field extension L/k and morphism X→Y, ∂(X_L/Y_L)⊆π⁻¹∂(X/Y); in particular scalar extension preserves boundarylessness. These assertions impose no smoothness or reducedness hypothesis.
